source_license: Public — official government data. Verify terms of use with Fairfax County before commercial redistribution.
pilot_notes: Live-verified 2026-08-15 via six rounds of disposable diagnostic GitHub Actions dispatch, the same methodology used for Loudoun and Prince William. Three rounds enumerating Fairfax County's own ArcGIS Server host (www.fairfaxcounty.gov/mercator, 8 REST folders) found nothing -- the real zoning service is instead hosted on ArcGIS Online's shared infrastructure under Fairfax's own official org account (FX.AuthData, contentStatus 'public_authoritative'), findable only via an ArcGIS Online item search. Layer 0 ('Zoning') carries real fields ZONECODE/ZONETYPE/PROFFER/PUBLIC_LAND/JURISDICTION, geometryType esriGeometryPolygon, 6,440 features total -- but that spans THREE real jurisdictions merged into one layer (Fairfax County, Town of Herndon, Town of Vienna, plus a few null-jurisdiction records). The fetch pipeline is configured with a where clause (JURISDICTION='FAIRFAX COUNTY') to scope to the county only: 6,242 features, 0 with null/empty ZONECODE, 44 real distinct ZONECODE values, independently confirmed. Do not treat an absent or 'not_listed' classification as meaning data centers are prohibited -- it means the classification has not been researched yet.
known_limitations: districts.json does not exist with researched names/categories yet -- every real zoning code returned by the live geometry will show as unclassified until permitted-use research is done against the actual ordinance.

The Zoning FeatureServer layer 0 has no separate district-name field -- ZONECODE is the only classification attribute. A coarse ZONETYPE grouping field exists (RESIDENTIAL/COMMERCIAL/INDUSTRIAL/PLANNED UNITS/OTHER/TYSON) but is not a per-code name and is not mapped into district_category.

The same FeatureServer also carries Town of Herndon and Town of Vienna zoning under the same layer -- deliberately excluded from this jurisdiction's data via a where-clause filter (JURISDICTION='FAIRFAX COUNTY') rather than ingested as county data.

Parcel-level zoning_code is not published by Fairfax County's parcel service -- connecting a parcel to this geometry requires a parcel-to-zoning spatial join, which does not exist in this codebase yet (planned, not yet built).
notes: Third Virginia pilot jurisdiction after Loudoun and Prince William. Geometry pipeline proven end-to-end; permitted-use classification research is the next step, not yet done.
